tests.case: desktop Details preserves all original width and height caps and the 410px prose measure

DetailsModalScaleTests.The_card_takes_ha.reason: Native Electron is resized through the ten exact source widths from 1200 to 7680. Each rendered card is measured against the original half-width/floor/ceiling formula, within Chromium's subpixel rounding.

tests.case: desktop Details preserves all original width and height caps and the 410px prose measure

DetailsModalScaleTests.The_card_takes_tw.reason: All six original heights from 640 to 2160 are exercised. Actual card height equals the 0.667 viewport cap with its 720px floor, further constrained by the original 40px top/bottom margins when the available viewport is shorter.

DetailsModalScaleTests.A_window_with_no_.reason: This assertion feeds zero, negative, NaN and infinity into Avalonia's ScaledLength binding converter before window layout. Electron has no scalar measurement binding or unmeasured-window callback: Chromium resolves viewport units when a native window attaches. Finite rendered geometry and the shipped cap floors are verified with the complete original real-window matrix; invalid CLR converter inputs have no corresponding UI input.

DetailsModalScaleTests.A_value_that_is_n.reason: The original assertion calls IValueConverter.Convert with null and a CLR target type. Electron uses CSS viewport lengths with no boxed-object conversion interface. Browser layout at the actual source window sizes is checked separately.

DetailsModalScaleTests.The_card_is_never.reason: This asserts that Avalonia IValueConverter.ConvertBack throws NotSupportedException. CSS size constraints have no reverse binding method. The native geometry matrix confirms that opening and laying out the Details card leaves the explicitly requested viewport dimensions intact.
